reading.body:
H.Res. 286 is a Democratic resolution of inquiry into DOGE's use of AI, with one sponsor and twenty-one cosponsors, all Democrats, and one lobbying filing naming it.

The pattern is a single-party instrument. Every named member belongs to the same party, so the resolution records an opposition position rather than a bipartisan one. A resolution of inquiry is a procedural demand for documents, not a statute, so its subject is what the executive branch did with AI and what it must hand over, not what AI may do.

The one lobbying filing comes from the National Treasury Employees Union, a federal employee union. That places the dispute over DOGE's AI use inside the federal workforce and the records it handles, which is where the resolution's language about private information and essential services points. The data does not say what position the union took, only that the bill was an issue in its filing.

What the data does not cover is the outcome. It records a latest status date of 2025-04-01 and no vote count, so nothing here shows whether the documents were transmitted or the resolution advanced. It also carries no text of the resolution itself, no committee action, and no second lobbying filing, so the reader cannot infer the scale of industry interest from a single union filing.
